items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: one of the influences was the influence of a trumpet player by the name of Bubber Miley and a trombone player by the name Charlie Irvis.

ctx.x: Yes, the Ellington sound is a development over many years, or -- and many influences. I believe -- I joined the band in '32, so it had been developed quite a bit

when I got there. But there seemed to be two or three influences that were the strongest, and one of the influences was the influence of a trumpet player by the name of Bubber Miley and a trombone player by the name Charlie Irvis.

Bubber Miley was a person who played with a plunger, and different mutes and got different effects. And Irvis was did the same thing on trombone, and the two of them were like a duo, and it sort of developed that they were a jungalistic type of music. Then the band became the accompaniment to this music.
